'''Reggie Christian Hearn''' (born August 14, 1991) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and current scout for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern Wildcats]].

==High school==
Hearn was an undersized post player while at [[R. Nelson Snider High School]], in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]], and he was lightly recruited by college programs and receive no D-1 scholarship offers.{{Citation needed|date=August 2024}}

==College career==
Hearn landed as a [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] at [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], for [[head coach]] [[Bill Carmody]], on a recommendation from [[Princeton Tigers men's basketball|Princeton]] head coach [[Mitch Henderson]]. He ultimately earned a scholarship, and became a standout player for the team, by his junior season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Powers |first1=Scott|title=NU's Hearn reflects on inspirational career|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/colleges/post/_/id/8988/northwesterns-hearn-reflects-on-inspirational-career?ex_cid=espnapi_public|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=[[ESPN.com]]|date=May 14, 2013}}</ref> As a senior, in the 2012–13 season, Hearn averaged 13.4 points and 4.6 rebounds per game, earning Honorable Mention All-[[Big Ten Conference]].

==Professional career==
===Idaho Stampede (2013–2014)===
Following his [[college basketball]] career, Hearn joined the [[Idaho Stampede]] of the NBA Development League (now called the [[NBA G League]]).

===Reno Bighorns (2014–2018)===
Hearn played for the Stampede for a full season, and part of another, before being traded to the [[Westchester Knicks]],<ref>{{cite news|last1=Marini |first1=Glenn|title=Snider Grad Hearn Traded From NBADL's Idaho To Westchester|url=http://wane.com/2015/01/27/snider-grad-hearn-traded-from-nbadls-idaho-to-westchester/|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=WANE.com|date=January 27, 2015}}</ref> and ultimately landing with the [[Reno Bighorns]]. With the Bighorns, he earned a reputation of one of the G League's top [[Three-point field goal|three-point]] shooters.

During the [[2016–17 NBA Development League season|2016–17 season]], Hearn was selected to compete in the three-point contest at the 2017 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Reggie Hearn to participate in NBA D-League three-point contest|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/reggie-hearn-to-participate-in-nba-d-league-three-point-contest/n-5233968|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=Oursportscentral.com|date=February 9, 2017}}</ref>

On October 10, 2017, Hearn was signed by the [[Sacramento Kings]] to a training camp deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Kings sign Reggie Hearn and David Stockton |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-hearn-stockton |access-date=October 10, 2017|work=[[Sacramento Kings]]|date=October 10, 2017}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2018)===
On January 15, 2018, Hearn signed a one-year, [[two-way contract]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2018/01/14/pistons-sign-reggie-hearn-two-way-deal/109466482|title=Pistons to sign G Reggie Hearn to two-way deal|access-date=April 27, 2018|date=January 14, 2018|work=[[Detroit News]]|author=Beard, Rod}}</ref> Hearn made his NBA debut on February 5, playing 2:33 in a 111–91 win against the [[2017-18 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]] and making a [[three point field goal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-reggie-hearn-makes-nba-debut-monday/|title=Pistons' Reggie Hearn: Makes NBA debut Monday|access-date=April 27, 2018|date=February 7, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> The points were the first NBA points by a former Northwestern Wildcat since [[Geno Carlisle]] in December 2004, the first by a Northwestern graduate since [[Evan Eschmeyer]] in the May 2003 and the first NBA three point shot by a Wildcat since [[Rex Walters]] in the January 2000 and the first by a Northwestern graduate since [[Billy McKinney (basketball)|Billy McKinney]] in 1981.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.insidenu.com/2018/2/6/16977758/reggie-hearn-first-nba-points-shot-detroit-pistons-northwestern-basketball-carlisle-eschmeyer|title=Reggie Hearn scores first NBA points, ending Northwestern's 13-year drought|access-date=April 27, 2018|date=February 6, 2018|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|author=Ragatz, Will}}</ref> Hearn appeared in a total of three games for the Pistons, but did not score again during the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-reggie-hearn-sees-three-games/|title=Pistons' Reggie Hearn: Sees three games|access-date=April 27, 2018|date=April 20, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>

===Stockton Kings (2018–2019)===
For the 2018–19 season, Hearn joined the [[Stockton Kings]] of the G League.<ref>{{cite web |title=STOCKTON KINGS WAIVE FOUR PLAYERS |url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-waive-four-players/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 3, 2018 |date=October 31, 2018 |archive-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809222623/https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-waive-four-players/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===South Bay Lakers (2019–2020)===
For the 2019–20 season, Hearn joined the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the G League.<ref>{{cite news |title= South Bay Lakers Set Opening Night Roster |url= https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-set-opening-night-roster-1920/ |access-date= November 7, 2019 |work= [[NBA.com]] |date= November 4, 2019 |archive-date= January 21, 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210121012818/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-set-opening-night-roster-1920/ |url-status= dead }}</ref> He posted 23 points, four rebounds, five assists, one steal and a block during a win against the [[Iowa Wolves]] on February 25, 2020. Hearn averaged 12.6 points and 3.4 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reggie Hearn: Scores 23 in win |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/reggie-hearn-scores-23-in-win/ |access-date=June 2, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 26, 2020}}</ref>

===NBA G League Ignite (2020–2021)===
In October 2020, Hearn signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]] as one of the veteran players to mentor younger prospects.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Taylor|first1=Cody|title=Reggie Hearn to join NBA G League Ignite with Jalen Green, others|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2020/10/18/nba-g-league-ignite-roster-reggie-hearn/|work=Rookie Wire|date=October 18, 2020|access-date=November 1, 2020}}</ref> He averaged 3.9 points and 2.6 rebounds in 13 games.<ref name="FraportSky">{{cite news|last1=Skerletic|first1=Dario|title=Fraport Skyliners sign Reggie Hearn|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fraport-skyliners-sign-reggie-hearn/|work=Sportando.basketball|date=August 25, 2021|access-date=August 25, 2021}}</ref>

===Memphis Hustle (2021–2022)===
On August 25, 2021, Hearn signed with [[Skyliners Frankfurt|Fraport Skyliners]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga|easyCredit BBL]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Reggie Hearn komplettiert den Kader der Fraport Skyliners|url=https://www.bblprofis.de/index.php/2021/08/28/reggie-hearn-komplettiert-den-kader-der-fraport-skyliners/|website=bblprofis.de|date=August 25, 2021|access-date=October 19, 2021|language=de}}</ref> However, on September 16, he parted ways with the team without playing a single game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Skyliners Frankfurt trennen sich von Flügelspieler Reggie Hearn|url=https://www.hessenschau.de/sport/basketball/skyliners-frankfurt/basketball-skyliners-frankfurt-trennen-sich-von-fluegelspieler-reggie-hearn,kurz-skyliners-hearn-100.html|website=hessenschau.de|date=September 16, 2021|access-date=October 19, 2021|language=de}}</ref> On October 23, he signed with the [[Memphis Hustle]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Moore|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2021-22 training camp roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster-211023/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 24, 2021}}</ref>

==National team career==
In 2017, Hearn was selected to the [[United States men's national basketball team|U.S. national team]] competing at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Reggie Hearn Named to USA Basketball Men's AmeriCup Team|url=http://nusports.com/news/2017/8/21/mens-basketball-reggie-hearn-named-to-usa-basketball-mens-americup-team.aspx?path=msoc|access-date=August 23, 2017|work=[[Northwestern Wildcats]]|date=August 21, 2017}}</ref> where he won a gold medal.

Hearn returned to team USA in 2018, playing on two World Cup qualifying teams. In five qualifying games, he averaged 12.2 points and 4.2 rebounds, while shooting 64% from three-point range. For his efforts, Hearn was named the 2018 [[USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Reggie Hearn named 2018 USA Basketball male athlete of the year|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/reggie-hearn-named-2018-usa-basketball-male-athlete-of-the-year/|access-date=December 9, 2018|work=[[NBA.com]]|date=November 28, 2018|archive-date=December 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209213344/https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/reggie-hearn-named-2018-usa-basketball-male-athlete-of-the-year/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
Hearn retired in 2022, joining the [[San Antonio Spurs]] as a scout.<ref>{{cite web| last = Ayen| first = Josh | url = https://www.wane.com/sports/local-sports/source-former-snider-standout-hearn-joining-spurs-scouting-department/ | title = Source: Former Snider standout Hearn joining Spurs’ scouting department | date = October 1, 2022| website = wane.com| publisher = WANE | access-date = November 21, 2023| quote = }}</ref>
